raw_response.publication_year_note: The cached 30-page PDF is an author manuscript (Page 1 extracted no text; Pages 2-30 contain the full manuscript, references, and appendices) with no journal header, online-first date, or volume/issue publication year printed anywhere in the text; latest internal data are from October 2023 and latest cited references are from 2023 (the prompt bibliographic header lists DOI 10.1007/s11269-024-04076-4).
raw_response.rationale: Study S166 proposes a six-dimension water and sanitation affordability assessment framework and applies deterministic arithmetic accounting formulas (Equations 1-10) to secondary SNIS utility, IBGE Census/PNADC income, CADUnico poverty registry, and October 2023 utility tariff/connection-fee schedules across 4,052 Brazilian municipalities served by state-owned providers (plus state capitals). Although it compares descriptive affordability ratios for low-income households with versus without social-tariff discounts (AR2 vs. AR3), social-tariff uptake rates, and connection-fee burdens relative to income thresholds, every output is a purely descriptive percentage or deterministic tariff-ratio calculation with zero inferential statistical tests, regressions, correlations, standard errors, confidence intervals, or p-values anywhere in the paper.
